summary: A 1920s cupola, a 1930s wood tower and a 1947 steel tower came before the present 1961 all-steel tower, now kept for emergency use.

facts.status_note: Kept for emergency use per the 2022 NHLR listing and firelookout.com; a 2016 blog labelled the site abandoned.

staffing.status: Not regularly staffed; last staffed in August 2003 for a brief spell of lightning; emergency use only

visit.trail_note: The final road is rough; a 2016 visitor stopped about 0.2 miles along it and walked the rest.

facts.agency: Oregon Department of Forestry (administers); U.S. Forest Service (cooperator)

events.note: Six miles of forest telephone line completed, connecting the Dale ranger station with the new Bone Point lookout station.
A small lightning fire was reported from Bone Point in July 1942.
30-foot steel live-in tower placed at Bone Point, one of ten surplus towers the state bought from World War II airfields (c.1947).
Keith Jenson listed as known lookout personnel.
Lookout cab sealed with plywood and painted inside; rock blasted near the top to widen the access road for supply trips.
Louise Stuart listed as known lookout personnel.
The present 30-foot all-steel live-in tower replaced the 1947 steel tower; NHLR gives 1961 as the build year.
Last staffed in August 2003 for a brief period of heavy lightning, though not regularly staffed for years before.

Forest Service Bone Point Repeater Placement project would move the radio repeater from the lookout building to a ground-level equipment building; decision signed August 14, 2014; project marked completed (move date not stated).
A blog visitor found the cab in no shape to live in and labelled the site abandoned.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, June 8, 2022.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 4,517 ft (1,377 m); firelookout.com and the 2016 blog give 4,527 ft. The story says roughly 4,500 feet. The brief's elevation_m of 1376.8 follows the NHLR figure.

The 2016 blog labels the site abandoned. The 2022 NHLR listing and firelookout.com both say it is kept for emergency use, so the record stays standing for emergency use and the story follows the later registry note.

A 1946 Coast and Geodetic Survey data sheet places the site in the Whitman National Forest; the NHLR and firelookout.com entries name the Umatilla National Forest. The story reports both without choosing a cause for the change.

notes_for_editor: The 1961 build date and the 2022 registration in the brief check out, and no corrections are needed. The 1920s cupola and 1930s wood tower have decade-only dates, so they have no event years. Access level is left unset because no source describes current public access or rental; the brief's access 'unknown' still stands. The 2016 'abandoned' label conflicts with the registry's emergency-use note; the record follows the newer source. Sources are hobbyist lookout sites plus NHLR and the Forest Service repeater project; no construction contract or agency history was found, so the reason for each replacement is unknown.
